grammar.title: Causative: get / have + objeto + particípio
grammar.explanation_pt:
Quando **outra pessoa** faz algo **para você** (geralmente um serviço pago), use o **causative**:

**get / have + objeto + particípio passado**
- I **got my hair cut**. (o cabeleireiro cortou — não eu)
- She **had her car washed**.
- We need to **get the roof repaired**.

Compare:
- "I **cut my hair**." = eu mesmo cortei (com tesoura em casa! ✂️)
- "I **got my hair cut**." = cortei no salão

**Get** é mais informal e comum na fala; **have** é um pouco mais formal. O sentido é o mesmo.

O causative funciona em **todos os tempos** — só muda o get/have:
- presente: I **get** my nails done every two weeks.
- passado: I **had** my eyes tested yesterday.
- futuro: I**'m going to get** my car fixed.
- present perfect: Have you **had** your passport renewed?
- modal: Where **can** I **get** this printed?

**Perguntas:** "Where **did** you **get** your hair **cut**?" / "Where can I **have** my shoes **repaired**?"

rows: I'm going to cut my hair.
I'm going to get my hair cut.

grammar.tip_pt: Expressões fixas muito úteis: **get your nails done** (fazer as unhas), **get a tattoo** (fazer uma tatuagem), **get your eyes tested** (fazer exame de vista), **get your teeth cleaned** (fazer limpeza nos dentes).

common_mistakes.wrong: I cut my hair yesterday. (no salão)
common_mistakes.right: I got my hair cut yesterday.
common_mistakes.why_pt: Se outra pessoa cortou, use o causative.

common_mistakes.wrong: I need to fix my car in the mechanic.
common_mistakes.right: I need to get my car fixed at the mechanic's.
common_mistakes.why_pt: O mecânico conserta: causative + at the mechanic's.

pronunciation.tip_pt: No causative, o particípio fica no fim e é bem audível. Lembre os três sons: **fixed** ("fikst"), **cleaned** ("klínd"), **painted** ("pêintid"). E **cut**, **done**, **made** são irregulares.

reading.title: The right to repair
reading.text: Have you ever had a phone repaired, only to be told that it's cheaper to buy a new one? You're not alone. For years, many manufacturers have made it difficult for customers to get their devices fixed: special screws, glued batteries, and parts that only official stores can buy. Now, a global movement called "Right to Repair" is fighting back. The European Union and several US states have passed laws requiring companies to sell spare parts and repair manuals for many products. Supporters say this will reduce electronic waste — one of the fastest-growing types of waste in the world — and save consumers money. In Brazil, small repair shops have always been part of the culture: we get our shoes resoled, our clothes altered and our appliances fixed. Maybe the rest of the world is finally catching up.

questions.q: What does the text say about Brazil?
questions.answer: Small repair shops have always been part of the culture.

grammar.title: prefer / would prefer / would rather
grammar.explanation_pt:
**Prefer** → preferência **geral** (sempre):
- prefer + **substantivo** + **to** + substantivo: "I prefer **tea to** coffee."
- prefer + **-ing** + **to** + -ing: "I prefer **walking to** driving."

**Would prefer ('d prefer)** → preferência **específica** (agora, nesta situação):
- 'd prefer + **to** + verbo: "I'd prefer **to stay** home tonight."
- 'd prefer + substantivo: "I'd prefer a window seat."

**Would rather ('d rather)** → preferência **específica**, muito comum na fala:
- 'd rather + verbo **base** (sem to!): "I'd rather **stay** home."
- comparação com **than**: "I'd rather **walk than take** the bus."
- negativa: "I'd rather **not** go."
- pergunta: "**Would you rather** watch a movie **or** go out?"

Resumo das estruturas:
- prefer A **to** B
- would prefer **to** do A (**rather than** do B)
- would rather do A **than** do B

reading.title: Introverts and extroverts at work
reading.text: Some people would rather work in a quiet room alone; others prefer a busy open office full of conversation. Psychologists often describe this difference using the terms introvert and extrovert. Introverts usually prefer deep one-on-one conversations to big group meetings, and many would rather write an email than make a phone call. Extroverts, on the other hand, often get energy from people and prefer brainstorming out loud. Most people, however, are somewhere in the middle — sometimes called ambiverts. The problem is that many workplaces are designed for extroverts: open-plan offices, constant meetings and team-building events. Smart companies now offer options: quiet zones, "no-meeting" days and flexible work. After all, people do their best work when they can choose how they work.

questions.q: What are ambiverts?

questions.q: What options do smart companies offer?

grammar.title: Verb + -ing / verb + to
grammar.explanation_pt:
**1. Verbos + -ing (gerúndio):**
enjoy, avoid, finish, mind, keep, give up, consider, suggest, miss, practice, can't stand, don't mind
"I **enjoy reading**." / "She **gave up smoking**." / "Do you **mind waiting**?"

**2. Verbos + to + verbo (infinitivo):**
want, need, decide, hope, plan, expect, agree, refuse, promise, learn, afford, manage, offer, would like
"I **want to travel**." / "They **decided to move**." / "I can't **afford to buy** a car."

**3. Preposição + -ing (sempre!):**
"I'm interested **in learning**." / "She's good **at drawing**." / "Thanks **for coming**." / "I'm thinking **of moving**." / "**Before leaving**, check the windows."
Atenção: **look forward to** e **be used to** terminam em preposição **to**, então pedem **-ing**: "I look forward to **meeting** you."

**4. Verbos que mudam de sentido:**
- **stop + -ing** = parar de fazer: "I **stopped smoking**." · **stop + to** = parar para fazer: "I **stopped to buy** water."
- **remember + to** = lembrar de fazer (antes): "**Remember to lock** the door!" · **remember + -ing** = lembrar de ter feito: "I **remember meeting** him in 2010."
- **try + to** = tentar (esforço): "I **tried to open** the jar." · **try + -ing** = experimentar: "**Try drinking** tea with ginger."

**5. Like, love, hate, start, begin, continue** → aceitam os dois com pouca diferença: "I like **swimming** / **to swim**."

examples.en: I've been considering moving abroad, but I can't afford to leave my job yet.
examples.pt: Tenho considerado morar fora, mas ainda não tenho condições de deixar meu emprego.

examples.en: Remember to send the report! — Don't worry, I remember sending it yesterday.
examples.pt: Lembre de enviar o relatório! — Não se preocupe, lembro de ter enviado ontem.

examples.en: I'm really looking forward to seeing you next week.

grammar.tip_pt: Aprenda esses verbos **em chunks**, não em listas: "enjoy doing", "want to do", "good at doing", "look forward to doing". Repetir os blocos é mais eficiente que decorar regras.

common_mistakes.wrong: I look forward to see you.

common_mistakes.why_pt: Look forward to + -ing (o to é preposição).

pronunciation.focus: Want to = "wanna", going to = "gonna", have to = "hafta"

lines.en: Want to build better habits? Here's my advice. First, avoid trying to change everything at once. Choose one habit and practice doing it every day. Second, stop waiting for motivation — it comes after you start, not before. Third, if you keep forgetting, remember to attach your new habit to an old one: "After brushing my teeth, I'll read for ten minutes." And finally, don't give up doing it if you miss one day. Nobody's perfect. I look forward to hearing about your progress!

reading.title: Why we procrastinate
reading.text: We all know the feeling: you need to finish a report, but you keep checking your phone, cleaning your desk, or watching "just one more" video. Most people think procrastination is about being lazy, but psychologists disagree. Research suggests that procrastination is mainly about avoiding negative emotions — boredom, anxiety, fear of failure. When a task makes us feel bad, our brain decides to look for something more pleasant. So how can we stop procrastinating? Experts suggest breaking big tasks into tiny steps ("open the document" instead of "write the report"), using a timer to work for just 25 minutes, and forgiving yourself for procrastinating in the past. Interestingly, people who forgive themselves are less likely to procrastinate again. Now, stop reading and go do that thing you've been avoiding!

grammar.title: Subject x object questions
grammar.explanation_pt:
Quando a pergunta é sobre o **objeto** (quem **recebe** a ação), use o auxiliar normal (do/does/did):
- "**Who did** you **call**?" → "I called **my mom**." (você ligou para alguém — quem?)
- "**What did** she **buy**?" → "She bought **a car**."

Quando a pergunta é sobre o **sujeito** (quem **faz** a ação), **não use auxiliar** — a question word **é** o sujeito e o verbo fica na forma afirmativa:
- "**Who called** you?" → "**My mom** called me." (alguém ligou — quem?)
- "**What happened**?" (❌ "What did happen?")
- "**Which** app **works** best?"
- "**How many people came** to the party?"

Compare:
- **Who loves** Ana? (alguém ama a Ana — quem?) → Pedro loves Ana.
- **Who does** Ana **love**? (a Ana ama alguém — quem?) → Ana loves Pedro.

**Perguntas indiretas** (mais educadas): depois de "Do you know...?" / "Can you tell me...?", use a ordem de **afirmativa**:
- "Where **is** the bank?" → "Do you know where **the bank is**?"
- "Who **did** you **call**?" → "Can you tell me who **you called**?"

reading.title: The power of word of mouth
reading.text: Who do you trust more: an advertisement or a friend? For most people, the answer is obvious. Marketing studies have repeatedly shown that personal recommendations are among the most trusted forms of advertising. That's why so many businesses invest in referral programs: "Recommend a friend and you both get 20% off." Online reviews have become a digital version of word of mouth — but they have a problem. Who writes them? Some companies pay for fake five-star reviews, and some competitors post fake negative ones. How can you tell what's real? Experts suggest reading the three-star reviews, which are often the most honest, looking for specific details, and checking whether the same reviewer has written many similar reviews. And, of course, asking someone you actually know.
